issues.problem: The prefilter takes the tool name with a greedy sed over the raw payload: 's/.*"tool_name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\(mcp__[^"]*\)".*/\1/p'. The greedy .* matches the LAST "tool_name":"mcp__..." in the line. Host payloads put tool_input after tool_name, and MCP tools that take a free-form object (GitHub actions_run_trigger 'inputs', and others) let the agent add a nested key, so a delivery call exits 0 before any gate runs.
issues.evidence: pmcp.sh: mcp__github__actions_run_trigger {method:run_workflow, workflow_id:deploy.yml, ref:main} -> DENY COMPLETION BLOCKED; the same with "inputs":{"tool_name":"mcp__x__get_y"} -> SILENT(allow). Escaped strings (a PR body containing the text) are not affected (still DENY).
issues.suggested_fix: Read the real top-level tool_name (jq -r .tool_name, or anchor the sed on the first occurrence / the key before tool_input), and only skip for names whose suffix is in a read-only allowlist. Add a test with a nested tool_name key.

issues.problem: R1-22 strict-everywhere still misses pushes that update the default branch or push a tag: the matching refspec ':' and glob refspecs (dst '' and 'refs/heads/*' are skipped), a tag created earlier in the same command (show-ref runs before the tag exists), and pushes run in another worktree via 'git -C <dir>' or 'cd <dir> &&' (HEAD/bare push are resolved against the hook's cwd).
issues.evidence: p22.sh on branch feat2 with main checked out in worktree wtmain: 'git push origin :' -> 'Intermediate commit allowed' and the real command moved remote main 880242a..6776412; "git push origin 'refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*'" -> intermediate, remote main 6776412..cb664e0; 'git tag v9 && git push origin v9' -> intermediate; 'git -C <wtmain> push origin HEAD', 'cd <wtmain> && git push origin HEAD', 'cd <wtmain> && git push', 'git -C <wtmain> push' -> intermediate (same commands with the hook cwd inside wtmain -> DENY).
issues.suggested_fix: Treat an empty destination (':' matching) and any destination containing '*' as default-branch pushes; treat a short destination that is not an existing branch as a possible tag when the same command creates a tag (or any 'git tag' in the analysis), or simply treat every non-branch bare name as a tag push; resolve HEAD/@/bare pushes against the analysed command's -C / cd directory (the analysis already tracks cwd for other checks) and fall back to delivery when the directory cannot be determined. Add test rows.

issues.problem: Under strict-everywhere, GitHub MCP writes that commit straight to the default branch stay intermediate: push_files, create_or_update_file and delete_file with branch=main need only the planning floor. The default-branch check reads only shell push refspecs.
issues.evidence: pmcp.sh (planning floor recorded, feature branch checkout): mcp__github__push_files {branch:"main"} -> 'Intermediate commit allowed'; create_or_update_file {branch:"main"} -> intermediate; delete_file {branch:"main"} -> intermediate.
issues.suggested_fix: For MCP write tools, compare tool_input.branch (missing branch = the repository default, so also delivery) with the default-branch names and promote to the completion tier; add tests.

issues.problem: The sandbox test checks SB_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR, which an agent can set for a nested host CLI together with SB_RUNTIME_PRESERVE_STATE_DIR=1 while keeping its real HOME. The child then has the user's auth, plugins and git credentials, but every gate honouring SB_AGENT_CERT_RUN is off. The doc comment's residual ('that child has none of the user's auth, plugins or state') is wrong for this spelling.
issues.evidence: env -i HOME=/root TMPDIR=/tmp SB_AGENT_CERT_RUN=1 SB_RUNTIME_PRESERVE_STATE_DIR=1 SB_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR=$P/tmpstate bash -c 'source runtime-paths.sh; source cert-bypass.sh; sb_cert_run_bypass_active' -> BYPASS (also with SB_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR=/tmp/x-nonexist). Same with HOME=/root and no override -> gated.
issues.suggested_fix: Also require SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT (derived from HOME) and HOME itself to be under a fixed temp root and not the passwd home; or ignore SB_RUNTIME_PRESERVE_STATE_DIR for the sandbox decision. Add a test with the preserve variables and a non-temp HOME.

issues.problem: The gh api release target is parsed only from separate '-f/-F/--field/--raw-field k=v' tokens of the FIRST gh api command. Other valid spellings fall back to origin/HEAD, so CI is checked for the wrong commit (the R1-19/R13-08 class).
issues.evidence: prel.sh (origin/main=416419a, red=79e57ab): '--field=target_commitish=<red>' -> 416419a; '-ftarget_commitish=<red>' -> 416419a; 'gh api user && gh api repos/o/r/releases -f tag_name=v9 -f target_commitish=<red>' -> 416419a; 'gh api -X POST repos/o/r/releases --input body.json' -> 416419a. Control: '-f target_commitish=<red>' -> 79e57ab.
issues.suggested_fix: Select the gh api command whose endpoint is .../releases, parse --field=/--raw-field=/-fKEY=/-FKEY= forms, and deny (cannot determine the release target) when the body comes from --input or when no target can be read from a releases POST.

issues.problem: The passwd-home exclusion uses getent, which macOS does not ship; there the check silently does nothing (harmless today because macOS homes are under /Users, but the documented guarantee does not hold).
issues.evidence: static: getent passwd ... 2>/dev/null | cut -> empty on macOS -> the case arm is skipped.
issues.suggested_fix: Fall back to python3 -c 'import pwd,os;print(pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir)' or eval echo ~$(id -un).
